rule.text: Settled = accuracy (correct / all uses, voice turns) at 80% or more in each of the last 4 sessions in a row, counting only sessions with at least 3 uses. A session with fewer uses neither helps nor breaks the streak. The Ledger suggests "settled"; Murat confirms.

shared_rules: Voice turns only; each use counts once.
A mistake corrected straight away counts as half.
Not counted: repeating a sentence Claude just modelled, quoting a text, or talking about the chunk.
If the transcript is unclear ("to" or "into"?), the use is dropped, not guessed.
later: January: Ledger review; decide how to handle collocations
Passives and subject-verb agreement, sliced the same way (e.g. "the data is just covers" -> "the data just covers")

items.title: "to" or "into" after add, put, paste, devote
items.counts: Every add / paste / devote / dedicate with its object and a following preposition phrase. "put" only with a list, notes, chat, document or system, or with effort, time or money.
left_out: physical placing ("put the box in the car")
phrasal verbs (add up, put off, put up with)

examples.wrong: add these points into that list
examples.right: add these points to that list

items.title: verbs with a fixed preposition, or none
items.counts: A closed list of 10, only when the word has its object or complement: approach, mention, research, contact, join, discuss (no preposition); remind of, responsible for, bored with / of, knowledge of.
left_out: nouns with their own preposition ("an approach to", "research on", "in contact with")

items.title: "to", not "for + -ing", for purpose
items.counts: A verb phrase saying why someone does something (= in order to).
left_out: "to" after want, need, try, decide (not purpose)
what a thing is for ("a tool for cutting" is correct)
items.note: Mistakes are easy to find; correct uses are hard for a script to separate from other "to + verb", so accuracy is rough.

items.title: no "a" before uncountable nouns
items.counts: Every use of a closed list of uncountable nouns.
left_out: "knowledge" and "practice" ("a good knowledge of" and "a practice" can be correct)

examples.right: some feedback / a piece of feedback

items.title: "still" goes before "have"
items.counts: Every "still" in a clause with have / has.

examples.wrong: I have still lots of way to take
examples.right: I still have a long way to go

items.title: "yet" → present perfect
items.counts: Every "yet" as an adverb: "not ... yet" and questions ("Has it ... yet?").
left_out: "not yet" on its own as an answer
items.note: May be too rare to reach 3 uses per session; review after two weeks.

items.title: "already" and "just" → present perfect
items.counts: "already", or "just" meaning "a moment ago", with a finished action.
items.note: Lowest priority: American English accepts the past simple; Murat follows British English, so these count as slips.

items.title: finished time → past simple
items.counts: A clause with a finished-time word: yesterday, last week / month / year / night / Monday, ... ago, in 2016, when I was...
left_out: "since last week" and "the last few days" (time still going on)

items.title: "for" and "since" for things still going on
items.counts: "for + a length of time" or "since + a starting point" for something still true now.
correct: I've been working at SOCAR for 15 years
wrong: I'm working at SOCAR for 15 years
left_out: finished periods ("I lived there for five years")
future plans ("I'm staying for two weeks")

examples.wrong: I'm working at SOCAR for 15 years
examples.right: I've been working at SOCAR for 15 years
